sentences.text: Revenue compounded 3.3% a year from $65.1 billion in FY2017 to $87.0 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F201].
The path was a step change rather than a straight line: revenue rose 4.8% in FY2020 and 7.3% in FY2021, then slowed to 2.3% in FY2023 and 0.3% in FY2025 [D147][D198][D302][D406].
FY2020's 4.8% growth came on a 4% unit volume increase, with high single-digit volume in North America and pantry loading from the COVID-19 pandemic [D147][P72].
FY2019 operating margin fell 11.9pp to 8.1% on a non-cash impairment charge for Shave Care goodwill and the Gillette intangible [D109][F23][P62].
Excluding that charge, operating margin has held between 20.0% and 24.3% every year, and FY2026's 22.7% sits just above the 22.1% window median [F22][F29][F30][D648].
The US was the growth engine: its share of revenue rose from 40.8% in FY2018 to 47.9% in FY2026 [D512][D534].
In FY2026 the US contributed just 0.1pp of the 3.3% growth while non-US contributed 3.1pp, as non-US sales grew 6.1% [D536][D457][D511][D510].
FY2026 net sales rose 3% on favorable foreign exchange of 2% and pricing of 1%, with unit volume and mix unchanged [P26].
Fabric & Home Care is the largest segment at 34.8% of revenue and added 0.8pp in FY2026, while Beauty added 1.3pp on 7.1% growth [D541][D543][D603][D602].
Operating income grew 4.1% a year against 3.3% revenue growth, but FY2026 operating income fell 3.4% while revenue rose 3.3% [F202][F201][D458][D457].
FY2026 operating margin of 22.7% is 1.6pp below FY2025's 24.3% window high and 0.6pp above the 22.1% median [F30][F29][D647][D648].
The FY2026 decline came from a 1.0pp hit from cost of revenue and a 0.6pp hit from SG&A, as gross margin fell on unfavorable category mix and marketing spending rose [D483][D485][P25][P5].
Cost of revenue was 49.8% of revenue in FY2026 versus 48.8% in FY2025, and SG&A was 27.5% versus 26.9% [D435][D384][D437][D386].
Net margin fell only 0.5pp to 18.4% because other non-operating income rose $922 million to $1.1 billion on the Glad joint-venture dissolution gain [D471][F50][P24][X108].
The effective tax rate edged up to 20.8% from 20.3% on lower excess tax benefits from share-based compensation [D443][D392][P23].
Operating cash flow of $19.6 billion was 1.22x net income in FY2026, and free cash flow of $15.1 billion was 0.94x, above the 1.02x window median for that ratio [F80][F40][D444][F100][D445][D660].
Free cash flow margin of 17.4% sits between the 14.4% window low and 20.5% high [D441][D652][D653].
Operating cash flow rose 10% as inventories consumed $641 million for safety stock and new products, partly offset by $919 million from higher payables [P3][D462].
Capex rose 16.9% to $4.4 billion, or 5.1% of revenue, and capex ran 1.40x D&A, the highest ratio in the window [D464][F90][D440][D446].
Net debt was $24.2 billion, or 27.8% of revenue, against a staples peer median net cash of -1.0% of revenue, ranking only the 33rd percentile of six peers [D450][D451][D677][D676].
The current ratio of 0.68x is below the 0.72x window median and near the 0.63x low, with working capital at -$12.5 billion [F180][D663][D661][F170].
Buybacks of $5.0 billion plus dividends of $10.2 billion were 100.7% of free cash flow, and the diluted share count fell 1.3% [X134][X144][D453][D476].
Long-term debt fell 8.6% to $22.8 billion while the current portion rose to $6.5 billion [F190][D468][X194].
The current ratio has been below 1.0x in every year of the window, ending at 0.68x in FY2026, so the negative working capital is structural rather than new [F180][F171][F177].
Buybacks and dividends exceeded free cash flow in FY2025 at 116.6% and FY2026 at 100.7%, funded partly by debt [D402][D453][R2].
Payout above free cash flow is sustainable only while operating cash flow holds near $19.6 billion, so a conversion slip would force a cut to buybacks [F80].
Watch operating margin: a print below the 22.1% window median would confirm the FY2026 erosion, while a return above 24.3% would reverse it [D648][D647].
Watch capex against revenue: a ratio above the FY2026 5.1% would extend the capital-intensity climb from the 3.7% FY2023 level [D440][D285].
Watch free cash flow against net income: a reading below the 1.02x median would signal the payout is stretching [D660].
